transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Start Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Mark Holloway (Southbridge CISO), Jenna Liu (IT Security Manager), Tom Reyes (Lead Backend Eng), Sara Campos (Compliance)

Summary: quick security posture intake focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs for a regulated payments company. In-scope: SOC2/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS options, data residency and retention windows.

Topics: SOC2 + ISO status, SAML/SSO and SCIM, RBAC and least privilege, audit log formats + retention, KMS HSM options and key custody, Private (VPC) networking requirements, POC benchmark asks.

[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, um thanks for making time. I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm the account lead on this. Quick intros?
[00:00:08] Mark: Mark Holloway, CISO at Southbridge Payments. We uh, are leading this evaluation.
[00:00:12] Jenna: Jenna Liu, IT Security Manager. We run infra and identity.
[00:00:00] Tom: Tom Reyes, backend, will help on the POC and the network side.
[00:00:20] Priya: Priya Shah, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll handle the arch and security details.
[00:00:25] Maya: Maya Chen, CSM, quick note I'll help coordinate artifacts.

[00:00:35] Alex: Great. Agenda: 1) current compliance posture at Southbridge, 2) key requirements for private/dedicated/hosted, 3) questions about SSO/SAML, RBAC, logging, KMS, 4) next steps.

[00:01:05] Mark: Quick primer: we're a payment processor, PCI scope sits with core payment stack, but we still need strong separation for any PII and tokenization services. Our security steering wants SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 as baseline, and we have an internal requirement for customer data to be encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys for certain flows.
[00:01:30] Alex: Understood. Redwood offers SOC 2 Type II — we can share the report — and we have an ISO attestation. We'll send both. For keys we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys via EKM/HSM integrations in Dedicated/Private.
[00:01:55] Jenna: When you say customer-managed keys — is that KMS in the cloud like AWS KMS with key policy, or do you offer HSM module integration? We need FIPS 140-2 level requirements for some vaults.
[00:02:10] Priya: Great question. For Hosted API we typically use our managed KMS but we offer bring-your-own-key via cloud KMS for Dedicated and Private. We also have partners for HSM-backed keys — we can support FIPS validated modules for keys used in encryption at rest. The technical difference is in Private we can put the key control inside your VPC/HSM or integrate via a vault proxy.
[00:02:40] Mark: Okay that helps. Also need to understand audit logging — what logs do you surface, retention windows, and whether logs include PII or tokenized IDs.
[00:02:50] Priya: Our standard logs include request metadata, model version, token counts, error traces, and redaction flags. For Hosted we redact high-confidence PII, but we recommend Dedicated/Private if you require zero retention of file payloads or strict control — Dedicated can be configured to not persist input payloads and to export audit logs to your preferred SIEM (SPLUNK, Datadog, Sumo).
[00:03:20] Tom: You mentioned export — is there a streaming logs pipeline? We use Kafka for ingestion and would prefer a push to our logging cluster.
[00:03:28] Priya: Yes, we can stream logs via secure syslog/HTTPS forwarders or push to S3 buckets in your account. We also support webhook-based delivery for lower-volume events.
[00:03:40] Jenna: What about RBAC? Our org requires role separation: developers can deploy models but can't change key policies, ops can manage infra, and compliance has read-only access to logs.
[00:03:50] Priya: Redwood's Console supports organization-level RBAC with roles and scopes. You can map SAML groups to roles via SAML and SCIM provisioning. There are pre-built roles (admin, dev, viewer) and custom roles. We also have audit trails for console actions.
[00:04:12] Mark: How mature is the SCIM/IDP integration? We run Okta and have Rules that provision groups.
[00:04:18] Alex: We've done multiple Okta integrations in enterprise customers. SCIM provisioning is supported; we can map Okta groups to RBAC roles and enforce session timeouts, MFA requirement. We'll capture the SAML metadata exchange and share configuration steps.
[00:04:35] Sara: On retention — we have contractual obligations to retain audit logs for 7 years in some cases, but we may only keep request payloads for 90 days. Does Redwood support long-term archival of logs?
[00:04:45] Priya: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we can ship audit logs to your long-term storage for multiple years. Hosted has a default retention (90 days) but enterprise add-ons can extend retention and archive to your S3.
[00:05:00] Mark: Ok. Another point: PCI scope — we cannot send raw cardholder data to third-party hosted endpoints. We will need to ensure tokenization is done in scope or on-prem.
[00:05:10] Alex: Understood. Many customers handle tokenization in their own environment and only send tokenized values to the model. For POC we can run with sanitized payloads and demonstrate the latency/cost. If you need complete isolation, Private deployment keeps all traffic within your network.
[00:05:30] Tom: Network-wise — Private deployment options mention VPC peering and direct connect. Can you do cross-account VPC peering or do we have to use transit gateway?
[00:05:40] Priya: We support several patterns: VPC peering, Transit Gateway, and PrivateLink-type setups depending on cloud provider. We'll share a recommended diagram. For peering we usually need CIDR plans and a few firewall rules and port ranges.
[00:05:55] Mark: Any independent pen tests or third-party attestations? We need to present that to auditors.
[00:06:05] Alex: We have third-party pen tests annually and can provide a summary. Full reports often require an NDA; we can coordinate with legal.
[00:06:15] Sara: About encryption in transit — are TLS mutual auth options available for Dedicated/Private endpoints?
[00:06:22] Priya: Yes, mTLS is supported for Private and Dedicated endpoints so you can enforce client certs for service-to-service traffic.

[00:06:40] [Marker: small cross-talk for a few seconds, audio glitch]

[00:06:50] Jenna: On SAML attributes — we need custom attributes for team/role mapping. Can Redwood accept custom claims?
[00:06:55] Priya: Yes, we support custom SAML attributes and can map them via the Admin Console. Also SCIM group sync will help keep roles consistent.

[00:07:30] Mark: What about data residency — our contracts require EU-only residency for EU customers. Do you offer region isolation?
[00:07:36] Alex: We offer region routing and the Private control plane can be instantiated in specific cloud regions. Hosted has region choices but Hosted customers share infra; Dedicated and Private give you stronger residency guarantees. We'll provide the region availability matrix.

[00:08:05] Tom: Performance question: if we add KV-cache or prefix caching in front of frequent token lookups, what's persistence of cache? Is that on the server or can it live in our environment?
[00:08:15] Priya: Redwood's caching is configurable. For Private, you can host the KV cache inside your VPC and manage eviction policies — for Hosted it's managed by Redwood. Note: I said KV cash earlier — sorry, KV cache.

[00:08:35] Jenna: Any rate limiting for Dedicated? We need throughput guarantees and burst behavior documented.
[00:08:42] Alex: Dedicated includes reserved capacity and burst options; we'll share the SLOs and latency targets. SLA details are in the contract but we'll provide the performance profile doc.

[00:09:10] Mark: On logging formats — do logs include full request/response payloads? We need the option to redact or not persist payloads.
[00:09:18] Priya: You can toggle payload persistence. Many customers disable payload persistence in Dedicated/Private and only keep metadata. For Hosted you can request higher privacy settings or go Private for zero-persist policies.

[00:09:45] Sara: Who has access to keys? If we use BYOK in AWS KMS, will Redwood ever have ability to decrypt? Need to make sure key policy prevents Redwood access.
[00:09:55] Priya: With BYOK in your account, you control the key policy — Redwood's service principal will only have permissions if you grant them. For Private deployments, keys can stay entirely in your control. We'll outline patterns in the KMS whitepaper.

[00:10:20] Tom: For the POC we'll likely do a Dedicated environment with customer KMS and Okta SAML. We need to test tokenization flows (sanitized) and measure tail latency.
[00:10:30] Alex: Sounds good. POC scope: 1) connect Okta SAML+SCIM for RBAC, 2) KMS integration with BYOK, 3) log forwarding to your SIEM, 4) run benchmark token flow with 100 rps.

[00:10:50] Mark: Timeline — we need legal and procurement in loop; procurement wants pricing and data processing addendum.
[00:10:58] Alex: We'll include DPA and the standard privacy terms in the pack. I'll get pricing for Dedicated/Private options and a comparison table.

[00:11:15] Jenna: A small technical point — session replay and console access logs, do those live in the same retention policy?
[00:11:21] Priya: Audit logs from the console are part of the audit trail and can be exported separately; retention can be configured independent of request payload retention.

[00:11:40] Mark: Any blockers on our side for a POC? We have an Okta admin, AWS account admin, and the network team. We may need an NDA for deeper artifacts.
[00:11:50] Alex: We'll send an NDA if needed before sharing redacted pen test reports. For the POC we can start with non-prod tokenized data without an NDA.

[00:12:05] Sara: Compliance: do you support evidence for audits — we need AWS artifact references and SOC2 control mappings.
[00:12:12] Priya: Yes, we can provide control mappings and the SOC 2 Type II report. For AWS artifacts we can summarize the cloud controls and provide guidance for shared responsibility.

[00:12:30] Tom: Small nit: latency for signing requests when using remote KMS — any measurable impact?
[00:12:36] Priya: For typical symmetric encryption and envelope encryption pattern there's a small latency added for key retrieval; we recommend caching envelope keys locally and limit calls to KMS for sign/unwrap. We'll include guidance and config defaults.

[00:13:00] [Short pause, attendees skim docs]

[00:13:10] Alex: Ok, recapping next steps: Alex share SOC2, ISO, pricing; Priya share network diagram and KMS patterns; schedule POC week of 10/27; Southbridge to share retention policy excerpt and point of contact.
[00:13:30] Mark: Sounds good. Any competitors you see in our RFP? We were talking to BigCloudAI and a boutique infra provider.
[00:13:37] Alex: Got it. We'll include a differentiation note on cost predictability and dedicated isolation.

[00:13:50] Jenna: One last Q — do you offer data residency guarantees in contract language?
[00:13:55] Alex: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can add data residency clauses. We'll have legal plug-in language for the DPA.

[00:14:10] Tom: Ok let's close — we'll await artifacts and set the POC schedule.

[00:14:18] Alex: Thanks everyone, will follow up with the package.
[00:14:22] Mark: Thanks all.

End transcript. Note: transcription is imperfect in places (speaker labels, small mis-hearings, and occasional stutters).
